in_hebrew.name: אילאריה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אילאריה (HaIlariah) – היא שם נשי המקורב ל'אל' (El), האלוהות. בראשית חזון (Daniel 10:13), הכריז המלאך: 'אילאריה, הקדוש'. השם מאזכור המלאך, האמונה והקדושה. בעברית, 'אל' נוטה להטית ימין. 'אילאריה' – נשים שקראו על ידי הקדושה, וקשר עם האל.  'אילאריה' – פירוש 'בת האל', 'בת המלאך' – כפי שהיא קרויה, 'אמונה' – 'בת' האדם – 'בת' – 'האב' – 'אל' – 'אילאריה' – 'בת' 'האב' 'אל' – 'אמונה'.

in_greek.name: Ἱλαρία
in_greek.meaning: δούλη του Θεού, η αγγελία, η πίστη, η αγιότητα
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἱλαρία (Ilaria) – Ὁ ἄγγελος Ἱλαρίας ὁ κατηγορούμενος (Daniel 10:13) – ἡ δούλη τοῦ Θεοῦ. Ἅπαντος τῶν Ἀγγέλων (Ἄγγελος Ἱλαρίας) – ἡ αγγελία, ἡ πίστη, ἡ αγιότητα. Ἱλαρία (Ilaria) – Ὁ ἄγγελος Ἱλαρίας – Ὁ ἄγγελος (Ἰλαρίας) – Ὁ ἄγγελος (Ἰλαρίας) – Ἰλαρίας. Ἰλαρίας – Ἰλαρία – Ἰλαρία, ἡ δούλη τοῦ Θεοῦ.

in_english.name: Illaria
in_english.meaning: servant of God, angel, faith, holiness
in_english.long_meaning: Illaria is derived from the Hebrew name 'El' meaning 'God' and the Greek word 'angelos' meaning 'messenger'. In the Bible, the angel Ilaria is referred to as a servant of God (Daniel 10:13). The name Illaria is associated with faith, holiness, and the angelic realm. In Christian tradition, Illaria is considered a symbol of devotion, loyalty, and spiritual guidance. Those bearing the name Illaria are often seen as having a strong connection to their faith and a desire to serve God.

biblical_reference.note: The angel Ilaria is mentioned in the book of Daniel as a servant of God.

data.cultural_impact: In ancient Rome, 'illarus' was a term used to describe a radiant or illuminated person, often in the context of a ruler or high-ranking official. This notion of illumination and radiance carried over into Christian tradition with the name Illaria. Today, this name is often given to girls believed to have the potential to be shining lights in their communities or families.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Illaria is a name symbolizing enlightenment, radiance, and spiritual illumination. It reflects the belief that every person has the potential to shine brightly with the light of God within them. This name also has ties to the biblical story of the Magi following a star to find the baby Jesus, reinforcing the idea of light leading the way to revelation and spiritual truth. Illaria is a reminder that just as a light shines in the darkness, so too can the spiritual light of an individual shine and bring hope and guidance to others.

historical_references.reference: According to medieval legend, Illaria was a Christian princess who was martyred during the persecutions of Emperor Diocletian (AD 284-305). She is said to have lived in Greece and was subjected to various tortures for refusing to renounce her faith. The legend also claims that she miraculously healed a leper, which led to her discovery and eventual martyrdom.
historical_references.time_period: Late 3rd century AD (persecutions of Emperor Diocletian)

historical_references.reference: The name Illaria also appears in the works of Dante Alighieri (1265-1321), specifically in his Divina Commedia. In this context, Illaria is a character in Purgatorio, where she is depicted as a penitent soul who died from love for her husband, having refused his request to leave him for another man.
historical_references.time_period: Late 13th - early 14th century AD (Dante's Divina Commedia)
